logic_node.action_detail: For patients with symptomatic (NYHA class II-III) stable chronic HFrEF (LVEF <= 35%) receiving GDMT including a beta blocker at maximum tolerated dose, in sinus rhythm with resting heart rate >= 70 bpm, ivabradine can be beneficial to reduce HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular death.

source_text: For patients with symptomatic (NYHA class II to III) stable chronic HFrEF (LVEF <= 35%) who are receiving GDMT, including a beta blocker at maximum tolerated dose, and who are in sinus rhythm with a heart rate of >= 70 bpm at rest, ivabradine can be beneficial to reduce HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular death.

logic_node.action: Consider digoxin for persistent symptoms despite GDMT
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF. Digoxin has not been shown to reduce mortality.

source_text: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF.

logic_node.action_detail: Digoxin is commonly initiated and maintained at 0.125 to 0.25 mg daily. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has low lean body mass. Higher doses (0.375-0.50 mg daily) are rarely needed.

source_text: Therapy with digoxin is commonly initiated and maintained at a dose of 0.125 to 0.25 mg daily. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has a low lean body mass.

logic_node.action: Use low-dose digoxin in elderly patients
logic_node.action_detail: In patients >70 years of age, use low-dose digoxin (0.125 mg daily or every other day) initially due to increased risk.

source_text: Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has a low lean body mass.

logic_node.action_detail: Serum digoxin concentration should be monitored. Risk of death is independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with significantly higher risk at concentrations >= 1.2 ng/mL and >= 1.6 ng/mL. Target serum levels below 1.2 ng/mL.

source_text: The risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with a significantly higher risk observed in those with concentrations >= 1.2 ng/mL and >= 1.6 ng/mL.

logic_node.action_detail: In selected high-risk patients with HFrEF (LVEF <45%) and recent worsening of HF (hospitalized within 6 months or recently received IV diuretics) already on GDMT, with elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP >= 300 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >= 1000 pg/mL in sinus rhythm), vericiguat may be considered to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death.

source_text: In selected high-risk patients with HFrEF and recent worsening of HF already on GDMT, an oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (vericiguat) may be considered to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death.

logic_node.action_detail: Patients with systolic blood pressure <100 mmHg were excluded from the VICTORIA trial of vericiguat. Vericiguat should not be used in patients with SBP <100 mmHg due to risk of symptomatic hypotension and syncope.

source_text: Patients on long-acting nitrates, with SBP <100 mm Hg, or eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded.

logic_node.action_detail: Patients with eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded from the VICTORIA trial. Vericiguat should not be used in patients with eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2.

source_text: Patients on long-acting nitrates, with SBP <100 mm Hg, or eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded.

logic_node.action_detail: Patients on long-acting nitrates were excluded from the VICTORIA trial of vericiguat. Concurrent use of vericiguat with long-acting nitrates should be avoided.

source_text: Patients on long-acting nitrates, with SBP <100 mm Hg, or eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded.

logic_node.action: Uptitrate beta blocker before considering ivabradine
logic_node.action_detail: Beta blockers should be initiated and uptitrated to target doses as tolerated before assessing resting heart rate for consideration of ivabradine. Only 25% of patients in SHIFT were on optimal beta-blocker doses. Given well-proven mortality benefits of beta blockers, optimize beta blocker first.

source_text: Given the well-proven mortality benefits of beta-blocker therapy, these agents should be initiated and uptitrated to target doses, as tolerated, before assessing the resting heart rate for consideration of ivabradine initiation.

logic_node.action_detail: Monitor for symptomatic hypotension (9.1% vs 7.9% in VICTORIA) and syncope (4.0% vs 3.5% in VICTORIA) when using vericiguat. Although not statistically significant, both were numerically higher with vericiguat.

source_text: Although not statistically significant, symptomatic hypotension (9.1% versus 7.9%; P=0.12) and syncope (4.0% versus 3.5%; P=0.30) were numerically higher in the vericiguat group versus placebo.
